newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - Feb 5.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Lumber trends were mixed through Tuesday with the overall pace of trade slower and the tone more cautious, Random Lengths said in its midweek update. Secondaries hesitated and dealers bought hand-to-mouth from distribution yards or reloads. Structural panel prices rose and plywood supplies tightened.
Talk about the Canadian lumber quotas picked up but still failed to stir buyers of Canadian S-P-F, Random Lengths said.

Western S-P-F sales were slow and prices of Std&Btr 2x4 and #2&Btr 2x6 slipped. A discount in futures, along with daily volatility in the contract, added to buyers' caution and an unwillingness to commit to any firm market course. Producers in British Columbia had about 17 percent of the province's annual fee-free quota left to ship in February and March. But talk about the quota picked up. Canada markets' pricing was sloppy.
Canada exports as of January 28 were at 25.7 percent of the Jan-Mar quarterly quota and 86.6 pct of annual April-Mar quota.

Eastern S-P-F markets were quiet and some prices softened. In the #1&2, 2x6 was a tough sell and dropped $5 while other widths held. The 2x4 8-foot studs weakened. Mills adopted various strategies to deal with the quota, with trade uneven.

Southern Pine sales were restrained. Buyers were selective but producers appeared convinced that a round of buying would ensue when weather improved and wood started moving from retail yards. Narrows of #2 showed cracks' 2x8&wdr held or edged up.
Inland sales of dimension were spotty. Secondaries tested mills' staying power but found most firm on their lists. In dimension, wides remained tight and prices edged higher.

Coast Hem-fir and dry Douglas fir trading was slow following active sales on Friday. Demand for Hem-fir #2&Btr 2x12 was strong but sales of 2x6 and 2x8 dragged. Strength in green markets pulled dry fir prices higher. The #2&Btr 2x8 truckloads sold as high as $500, Random Lengths said.
